issues.body: The new error-status validation calls `(result.get("error") or "").strip()`. A corrupt result such as `{ "status": "odre-error", "error": 1 }` or a list-valued error raises AttributeError, bypassing the documented input-error path and its diagnostics. This remains fail-closed—no report is written—so it does not preserve the prior agreement-coverage vulnerability, but malformed input should be rejected deliberately rather than crashing.
issues.fix_hint: Require `isinstance(result.get("error"), str)` and a non-empty stripped value before accepting an error-shaped result. Add one self-test mutation with a non-string error and assert exit 2 with no report written.
issues.title: Non-string error fields crash the input gate instead of producing exit 2

verdict.summary: Round 3 resolves the prior major fail-open issue. For a present ODRE run, input_errors now rejects missing, skipped-no-odre, unknown, and malformed result statuses; requires allow/deny for ok results; requires error text for error-shaped results; and the end-to-end self-test proves these mutations exit 2 without writing a report. The absent-run mirror is also checked. One minor robustness issue remains: a truthy non-string error field raises AttributeError during validation rather than being reported as a controlled input error, but it still fails closed and cannot publish a partial agreement report. Progress is improving because the prior major finding is fixed and only this lower-severity input-diagnostics issue remains.
